author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-11-14 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: What I tell you is true.
context_before: I have come to speak of the true knowledge of God.
context_after: There is an inmost center in us all where truth abides in fullness. One called Jesus Christ is that center, saying: “I am the truth.” He has resurrected in me, broken the shell, and, as he came out I was set free. Night after night I become more and more aware that I am the creator of it all.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Knowledge Of God (1969-11-14).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-11-14 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Because life is in the blood.
context_before: The figure 1,150 is important here as it totals the number tone [sic] seven, which is Spiritual perfection. In his 6th chapter, John speaks of bread as “my body,” saying: “Unless you eat my body and drink my blood you have no life in yourself.” Why?
context_after: Here is a perfect vision of the symbolism of scripture. She has completely accepted the truth that the body of God is her own wonderful human imagination. Life (blood) is flowing forth from her now, as she has accepted her imaginal body in its fullness and blames no one else now, for she knows he is only herself. When you reach the point where you cannot blame another because you have accepted your imagination as the sole cause of the phenomena of life, you have eaten the loaf and drank the blood.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Knowledge Of God (1969-11-14).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-11-14 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Then, as she watched, I died.
context_before: A lady, whose eyes are now open as an incurrent witness, saw me dying. In her vision she told her friend not to touch me, for if she did I would not be set free.
context_after: These are wonderful visions for her to have, for “Unless I die thou canst not live. But if I die I rise again and thou with me. Wouldst thou love one who never died for thee? Or ever die for one who has not died for thee? And if God dieth not for Man and giveth not Himself eternally for Man, Man could not exist. So God died.” I have awakened from the dream of life. I have been born from above, and the only one who is born from above is God, He who perpetually dies. Her vision was perfect, and I cannot congratulate her enough.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Knowledge Of God (1969-11-14).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-11-14 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: That is not the truth of which the scriptures speak.
context_before: I am not speaking of anyone on the outside.
context_after: It makes no effort to change society, but rather urges all to “Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar’s.” He doesn’t try to make the slave a free person, but leaves him just as he is. Today all of our energies are going into keeping records and changing things. I recently received a notice from the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare. I thought they were interested in my health, and since I have been paying their insurance since 1936, I went to see them today. The lady asked me many questions, none of which were related to my health. She said she knew everything else about me, which confirmed my suspicions that we are all computerized numbers. She needed proof that I would be 65 this coming February. I showed her my passport, for I have no driver’s license as I do not drive, but she wanted a birth certificate. I told her that on the island and in the year I was born, a birth certificate was too expensive; but I was baptized and somewhere I have that certificate. She urged me to write for it, and I will; but our visit made me realize that everything about the garment you wear is already known by the government, all carefully computerized and filed.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Knowledge Of God (1969-11-14).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-11-14 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Take a glorious concept of life.
context_before: Can you imagine what it would be like if you were the man (the woman) you would like to be? Sustain that imaginal act as though it were true, and no power in the world can stop it from becoming true, because there is no other power. Try it beginning tonight.
context_after: Nothing less than the very best, and simply imagine it to be true about you and those you love. Start with your immediate circle and – although at the moment your circle may deny it by reason of what they are doing – persist in your assumption as though it were true, and it will harden into fact.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Knowledge Of God (1969-11-14).
